Title: Differentially private synthetic data generation for robust information fusion - ScienceDirect
# Differentially private synthetic data generation for robust information fusion. The framework for private synthetic data generation and utilization in information fusion. To maximize the benefits of synthesis data while ensuring data security, we propose a novel framework for the generation and utilization of private synthetic data in information fusion processes. Our results demonstrate that trading off weights contained in the differential privacy fine-tuning parameters can improve model performance, even achieving generation quality competitive with differential privacy full fine-tuning diffusion model. In recent years, deep learning-based image fusion techniques have gained considerable attention, particularly those employing generative adversarial networks [8], [9], autoencoder frameworks [10], and diffusion models [11]. Nevertheless, recent works [25], [26] have revealed that generative models can memorize and leak private feature of training data owing to the high capacity of deep neural networks. Training generative models with differential privacy is more challenging. Scaling up differential privacy into generative models [17], [18], [31] inspired by DP classifiers to defend against privacy attacks (e.g. membership inference attacks, reconstruction attacks and attribute inference attacks) and prevent attackers from inferring information about training samples from publicly available model parameters, while ensuring that the synthetic datasets are still useful for various downstream tasks. Meanwhile, we train the model using differentially private stochastic gradient descent to protect the privacy of the original data. We provide a novel image fusion framework based on synthetic data, which improves the robustness and accuracy of the fusion process, especially in scenarios with partially missing or privacy-restricted modalities. In this section, we introduce differentially private adaptive low-rank adaptation fine-tuning (DP-AdaFit), a method to train model with differentially private parameter efficient fine-tuning. In experiments, we choose guided-diffusion [24] as our default model, which achieves SOTA in the current literature of differentially private image generation. In this paper, we propose the framework that enhances the information fusion process by leveraging synthetic data generated through diffusion model. Next, we explore the impact of various model parameters on performance when training diffusion models with DP-SGD, and propose DP-AdaFit, a method significantly reduces the amount of noise without compromising privacy guarantee. ### Differentially private diffusion models generate useful synthetic images.

results.content: A **.gov** website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/differentially-private-synthetic-data. # Differentially Private Synthetic Data. In this series, we've examined several different ways to answer queries over data using differential privacy. So far each approach requires changing the way we answer queries - usually by adding noise to the answer - and modifying the tools we would normally use for analyzing data. The answer is “yes”: using techniques for generating *differentially private synthetic data*. It's important to note that many techniques for generating synthetic data do not satisfy differential privacy (or any privacy property). Differentially private synthetic data has a huge advantage over other approaches for private data analysis: as shown in Figure 1, it allows analysts to use any tool or workflow to process the data. This property makes differentially private synthetic data much easier to use than the approaches we have discussed previously--all of which require modifying the tools and workflows used to analyze data.
